newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurer makes 48 mln marks write-off.
newsitem.headline: German insurer makes 48 mln marks write-off.

text.p: Koelner Postversicherung VVaG (KPV), the Cologne-based mutual, has had to write off some 48 million marks in connection with real estate deals, the company told Reuters on Tuesday.

"Because of the development in the commercial real estate market, it has proved necessary for Koelner Postversicherung to make charges of 48 million marks in the 1996 accounts," Alfred Waiss, chairman of the management board, said.
The board member responsible for investment, Dieter Hajek, left the insurer at the end of 1996, KPV said.
Waiss said there had been irregularities in some real estate transactions, but refused to make any further comment.
He was also not prepared to say whether criminal charges would be brought against anyone.
Waiss has been chairman of the board in Cologne since April 1997. He also holds the same post at Vereinigte Postversicherung in Stuttgart, with which Koelner Postversicherung has formed a group.

The total investments of Koelner Postversicherung rose in 1996 from 3.8 billion marks to 4.2 billion marks. In view of such sums, even a serious loss of 48 million marks would have no drastic effect for insured members, insurance sources said.
Nevertheless, the company will have to realise a large part of its hidden reserves if it is to achieve a profit for 1996.
In 1995, the insurer had premium income of 418 million marks. For 1996, Waiss said he expects 425 million marks.

The group, formed in April 1997 with Vereinigte Postversicherung, has annual premium income of around 1.1 billion marks. In 1998, the two companies plan to merge. Both have their roots in post office staff insurance.
